title: Bahariya Formation, Egypt (Spinosaurus type locality)
summary: In 1912 collector Richard Markgraf found a partial Spinosaurus skeleton in the Bahariya Oasis of western Egypt, named S. aegyptiacus by Stromer in 1915. The early Cenomanian Bahariya Formation (about 97 million years old) was a coastal plain of lagoons, tidal flats and mangroves, with Carcharodontosaurus, Bahariasaurus, Aegyptosaurus and Paralititan. The holotype was destroyed in a 1944 bombing raid on Munich.

uncertainty.note: Smith et al. (2006) give early Cenomanian, about 97 Ma; Lacovara et al. (2001) say Cenomanian. Bounds here are the whole Cenomanian from the ICS chart, wider than the early-Cenomanian estimate.

as_recorded.value: early Cenomanian, about 97 million years ago

beats.caption: About 97 million years ago the Bahariya region was a low coastal plain of lagoons, tidal flats, mangroves and channels.
In 1912 fossil collector Richard Markgraf found the Spinosaurus remains at El-Bahariya, and Stromer named them Spinosaurus aegyptiacus in 1915.
Stromer’s original material was destroyed in an Allied bombing raid on Munich in April 1944.
